CANONICAL_NAME.value: UMDHMM 1.02 -- Hidden Markov Model toolkit in C: forward, backward, Viterbi and Baum-Welch (Tapas Kanungo, 1998)

VERSION.value: UMDHMM 1.02 (VERSION file); mirror github.com/palanceli/UMDHMM master (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: Rabiner's 1989 tutorial algorithms implemented directly in C at the University of Maryland (1998): esthmm TRAINS an HMM from an observation sequence by Baum-Welch (EM), testfor/testvit evaluate and decode, genseq samples. The classic compact reference many later toolkits cite; complements the vault's decode-only viterbi-hmm-xukmin. Preserved from a GitHub mirror of Kanungo's original distribution (the author's page is gone) -- HISTORICAL_ARCHIVE_MIRROR.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: unsupervised learning of a hidden Markov process

value.built_to: learn the transition and emission probabilities of a hidden process from its outputs alone, then decode the hidden states
value.pressure: hidden state with no labels; local optima of EM; sequences long enough for probabilities to underflow (scaling)
value.success_means: the trained model reproduces the generating model's parameters (up to relabelling) and its likelihood on held-out data

value.pressure: hidden state, unlabeled observations, numerical underflow
value.failure_condition: EM converges to a poor local optimum or the likelihood underflows without scaling
